title: Add Datadog Logs destination adapter + audit tag/facet mapping
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Summary: This PR adds a Datadog Logs destination adapter to the audit-log-exporter and establishes a stable mapping from audit event schema v2 -> Datadog tags/facets. It also introduces rate-limit aware batching behavior (primarily for 429/503) so we degrade gracefully under Datadog intake constraints while preserving at-least-once semantics. Context: As part of the SIEM-ready audit export beta, we support Splunk HEC, S3, and Datadog Logs. Datadog differs from Splunk in that (a) intake is strongly rate-limited, and (b) the best user experience is via consistent tagging/faceting for filtering/dashboards in Datadog. This PR aligns with ENG-5156 and the delivery semantics ADR (at-least-once, downstream dedup via event_id). Design notes (high-level): Adapter: Adds `datadog_logs` destination type with `site`, `intake_path`, and `api_key_secret_ref`. We send batches to `https://http-intake.logs.{site}/api/v2/logs` (default) with JSON payloads. Each audit event becomes one log item with a message, attributes, and tags. Tag/facet mapping: We map audit event fields into a consistent set of Datadog tags for filtering. Primary tags: `redwood.tenant_id`, `redwood.workspace_id`, `redwood.category`, `redwood.action`, `redwood.resource_type`, `redwood.actor_type`, and optionally `redwood.actor_id` (only when allowed by audit policy). We also set `service=redwood-audit-export`, `ddsource=redwood`, and `env=<region|deployment>` (exporter runtime env). We keep the raw payload minimal: we do not include request bodies, prompt text, or free-form metadata; event context is limited to schema v2 allowed fields and pre-existing redactions. Rate-limit aware batching: The adapter maintains a per-destination adaptive batch size. On 429, we back off with jitter and reduce batch size (floor 1). On success, we slowly increase toward the configured max (AIMD-like behavior) to recover throughput without oscillation. We also respect `Retry-After` when present and otherwise default to exponential backoff using the exporter retry policy. Checkpointing/dedup: We do not attempt exactly-once delivery. Each log item includes `event_id` as `redwood.event_id` (tag + attribute) so customers can dedup. We preserve ordering within a partition best-effort but do not guarantee strict order under retries. Security/PII: The adapter redacts sensitive fields in logs and avoids logging payload contents. Exporter logs include only: destination id, batch size, response status, dd request id (when provided), and retry wait. API key is loaded via secret ref; no key material in config logs. Tests: Adds unit tests for tag mapping (category->tag), and integration-ish tests via stubbed intake server covering 200, 429 with Retry-After, and 503 transient errors. Operators: Adds additional metrics for adapter status codes and rate-limit backoff behavior to help SRE tune defaults. Rollout: Feature-flagged behind destination validation at control plane; exporter supports the destination type when present in config sync. Follow-ups: (1) support additional Datadog intake paths for Gov/US3 sites (config already allows override); (2) add customer-facing docs and a Console “Test connection” for Datadog (tracked elsewhere).
commits: adapter/datadog: implement v2 logs intake client + request/response handling
mapping: add audit schema v2 -> dd tags/facets mapping helpers
retry: add rate-limit aware batch sizing + Retry-After support
metrics: add datadog adapter counters + backoff gauges
tests: add mapping unit tests + stubbed intake tests
docs: update destination type registry + local dev examples
notable_diff_snippets: Rate-limit behavior: on HTTP 429 -> if Retry-After present, sleep that duration; else exponential backoff (base=1s, max=60s) with jitter; reduce batch_size = max(floor, ceil(batch_size/2)); on success -> increase batch_size by +10% up to configured max.
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we standardize the tag keys to avoid later migration? In other exporters we use `redwood.category` not `category`. Also please ensure `event_id` is present both in tags and as a structured attribute for facet creation. Caleb Johnson (author): Updated mapping to always prefix `redwood.` and added `redwood.event_id` as both tag + attribute. Also added a unit test asserting presence. Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we’re not sending user agent / IP in a way that violates the audit PII policy. Datadog is not a “safe sink” by default for verbose fields. Also make sure exporter logs never include the payload. Caleb Johnson (author): Verified: payload includes only schema v2 allowed fields. IP/user_agent are only included when present in the canonical audit event and already subject to redaction rules upstream; this adapter does not add new fields. Exporter structured logs now explicitly omit payload and only log `dd_request_id`, status, and counts. Added a test that logger does not emit the serialized request body. Sean Gallagher (review): Rate-limit aware batching looks good but I’m concerned about thundering herd across tenants when DD is down. Do we have per-destination jitter? Also please add a metric we can alert on to detect sustained 429s. Caleb Johnson (author): Added jitter to all retry sleeps (full jitter capped by base delay). Added `audit_export_adapter_rate_limited_total{adapter="datadog"}` and a gauge `audit_export_adapter_backoff_seconds{adapter="datadog"}`. Colin O'Donnell (review): Customer expectation: they’ll want to filter by category/action quickly in Datadog. Can we include `action` as a top-level attribute too (not just tag), so facets are straightforward? Caleb Johnson (author): Added `redwood.action` attribute mirror alongside tag. Also added docs note on creating facets in Datadog for `@redwood.action` and `@redwood.category`.
release_notes: Enterprise: Audit log export now supports Datadog Logs as a destination (beta). Includes consistent tag/facet mapping for audit categories/actions and improved handling of Datadog intake rate limits (429/503) with adaptive batching + backoff.
